Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 53f2cb491b500897a619ff6abd72f565933760f0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2023 22:44:47 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] tls: fix NULL deref on tls_sw_splice_eof() with empty record

syzkaller discovered that if tls_sw_splice_eof() is executed as part of
sendfile() when the plaintext/ciphertext sk_msg are empty, the send path
gets confused because the empty ciphertext buffer does not have enough
space for the encryption overhead. This causes tls_push_record() to go on
the `split = true` path (which is only supposed to be used when interacting
with an attached BPF program), and then get further confused and hit the
tls_merge_open_record() path, which then assumes that there must be at
least one populated buffer element, leading to a NULL deref.

It is possible to have empty plaintext/ciphertext buffers if we previously
bailed from tls_sw_sendmsg_locked() via the tls_trim_both_msgs() path.
tls_sw_push_pending_record() already handles this case correctly; let's do
the same check in tls_sw_splice_eof().

Fixes: df720d288dbb ("tls/sw: Use splice_eof() to flush")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: syzbot+40d43509a099ea756317@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jann Horn <jannh@google.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20231122214447.675768-1-jannh@google.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/tls/tls_sw.c b/net/tls/tls_sw.c
index a78e8e722409..316f76187962 100644
--- a/net/tls/tls_sw.c
+++ b/net/tls/tls_sw.c
@@ -1232,11 +1232,14 @@ void tls_sw_splice_eof(struct socket *sock)
 	lock_sock(sk);
 
 retry:
+	/* same checks as in tls_sw_push_pending_record() */
 	rec = ctx->open_rec;
 	if (!rec)
 		goto unlock;
 
 	msg_pl = &rec->msg_plaintext;
+	if (msg_pl->sg.size == 0)
+		goto unlock;
 
 	/* Check the BPF advisor and perform transmission. */
 	ret = bpf_exec_tx_verdict(msg_pl, sk, false, TLS_RECORD_TYPE_DATA,
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/tls/tls_sw.c`**
- Added a check in the `tls_sw_splice_eof()` function to verify if the `msg_plaintext` size is zero. If it is, the function will now exit early by going to the `unlock` label, preventing further processing that could lead to a NULL dereference.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification in `tls_sw_splice_eof()` aligns with the existing behavior in `tls_sw_push_pending_record()`, which already handles cases where the plaintext or ciphertext buffers may be empty. This change ensures consistency in handling empty buffers across these functions, thereby preventing potential crashes due to NULL dereferences when the function is called in scenarios where the buffers are empty, such as during the execution of `sendfile()`. The patch addresses a specific bug reported by syzkaller, enhancing the robustness of the TLS implementation in the kernel.
